literal: Even the shade of many umbrellas, under their own umbrella, they will see—those who have the shade of possessing ears of grain.
translation: Those who live under the shade of the grain-yielding plough will see the sovereign umbrellas of many other kings brought under the shade of their own ruler's umbrella.
modern: நெற்கதிர்களை உடைய உழவுத் தொழிலின் நிழலில் வாழ்பவர்கள், பல அரசர்களின் குடை நிழல்களையும் தங்களது அரசனுடைய குடை நிழலின் கீழ் வரக் காண்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme political and economic power that stems from agriculture. The umbrella (குடை) is a classical symbol of royal sovereignty and protection. The poet states that those who work under the 'shade of grain' (அலகுடை நீழலவர்), meaning the farmers, ultimately empower their own king to bring all other rulers under his dominion. Because every kingdom depends on food for survival, a nation with a thriving agricultural base naturally commands the allegiance and respect of other states.
